issue_paraphrase: When a git remote is written in scp-like form without a protocol prefix and without a trailing .git, and the organization or repository name contains a dash (for example git@code1.somecompany.internal:somecompany-eval/owasp-juice-shop), Semgrep fails to convert it into the https URL used to link to findings. The recorded repository URL keeps the raw ssh-style form, so links shown for the report are broken. URLs that include an explicit protocol or end in .git parse correctly.
fix_summary: Rewrote the fallback regexes in cli/src/semgrep/external/git_url_parser.py: added '(?!\w+\://)' negative lookahead so scp-like URLs match the protocol-less branch, extended owner/name character classes with '~', made the name class lazy ([\w\-%~\.]+?) with optional trailing .git and '/'. Synced from the proprietary repo; also moved/expanded test_meta.py into cli/tests/default/unit/.
notes: Pure-Python fix; no OCaml build needed. The failing input is self-contained (no network). Reproducing requires the semgrep_interfaces submodule to be initialized before import. Full suite needs the compiled semgrep-core binary; the tests used here run in <0.1s at 1 CPU.

issue_paraphrase: In GitLab CI, the CI job token is embedded in the git remote URL as credentials (https://gitlab-ci-token:glcbt-...@gitlab-host/...). When Semgrep reads the project URL to record where rules or findings came from (for example when publishing rules), the full token is copied into the metadata and can end up in published artifacts. The reported repository URL should have the credentials stripped, keeping only host and path.
fix_summary: Added clean_project_url() in cli/src/semgrep/git.py: urllib.parse.urlsplit on the remote URL, then regex-strips everything up to the last '@' in the netloc (the credentials) and reassembles. get_project_url() now routes its result through the cleaner. An OCaml counterpart (libs/git_wrapper/Git_wrapper.ml) received the same change; the OCaml part is not needed to reproduce the Python bug.
notes: Pure-Python fix plus an unrelated OCaml counterpart; only the Python side is needed to reproduce. Repro needs a local git repo with a credentialed remote (git ls-remote --get-url does not hit the network). Requires semgrep_interfaces submodule initialized. Runs in <1s at 1 CPU.

install_recipe: cd /work/semgrep && git config --global --add safe.directory /work/semgrep && git reset --hard <sha> && git clean -fd && git submodule update --init cli/src/semgrep/semgrep_interfaces && python3 -m pip install -e ./cli && python3 -m pip install pytest pytest-mock pytest-snapshot
issue_paraphrase: Semgrep secrets findings that go through validation have two configuration knobs: the rule's general block/monitor action and per-state block/monitor actions for the validation states valid/invalid/error. Previously, setting the rule's general action to 'block' made every validation state block CI, even when the per-state action for that state said 'monitor'. A validator rule configured only to block one state therefore blocked everything; the per-state action should be the only thing consulted when a validation state exists.
fix_summary: In cli/src/semgrep/rule_match.py, is_validation_state_blocking now special-cases out.NoValidator (falls back to dev.semgrep.actions) and otherwise only consults dev.semgrep.validation_state.actions keyed by the mapped state; is_blocking for the validation-state branch returns is_validation_state_blocking alone instead of OR-ing in the general dev.semgrep.actions flag.
notes: Pure-Python fix, no OCaml binary needed, no network. Constructing a RuleMatch by hand needs the semgrep_output_v1 types, which is why the project's own parametrized unit test (create_validator_rule_match) is the cleanest oracle. Needs semgrep_interfaces submodule. Do not install pytest-freezegun on python 3.12 (imports distutils, breaks collection); pytest-mock and pytest-snapshot are required by other tests in the same file. Runs in <1s at 1 CPU.

install_recipe: cd /work/semgrep && git config --global --add safe.directory /work/semgrep && git reset --hard <sha> && git clean -fd && git submodule update --init cli/src/semgrep/semgrep_interfaces && python3 -m pip install -e ./cli && python3 -m pip install pytest
issue_paraphrase: For repositories hosted on Azure DevOps, the git URL contains a _git path segment (for example https://test@dev.azure.com/test/TestName/_git/Core.Thing). When Semgrep rebuilds the project URL from such a remote, whether configured via the SEMGREP_REPO_URL environment variable or discovered from an Azure remote origin, the _git segment is silently dropped from the URL, so links to findings in the web view point at a page that does not exist. The segment should be kept in the final URL.
fix_summary: The parser now records the azure_git_dir ('/_git') when stripping it from the owner, and get_url_from_sstp_url re-appends result.azure_git_dir when rebuilding the https URL, so the _git segment is preserved in URLs while still being removed from the repository name.
notes: Pure-Python fix, no OCaml binary or network. Takes any Azure-style URL with '_git' in the path; parsing happens purely locally. Requires semgrep_interfaces submodule. The test file lives under cli/tests/default/e2e-pro/ but only uses semgrep.meta and the parser, so no binary is needed. Runs in <1s at 1 CPU.
